claim_removed: The adopted t5 entry's C_interaction reference-card text called the flyer>media>SNS tie-break ordering '一般的な効果の強さ（実際のイベントで比べた記録による）' (general/universal effectiveness strength, based on a record of comparing actual events) — this claimed the ranking represents a measured comparison of the 3 COMPOSITE plans' overall effectiveness.
cited_source: 竹内裕二（2023）表4「イベントを知った情報源」(cited in research.md and fact_sheet.json's sources)
source_does_not_support_because: The cited study measured self-reported information sources among N=334 attendees for ONE documented event (chirashi=148, TV=116, SNS-total=22) -- it did not measure comparative effectiveness of the three COMPOSITE plans this game presents. The middle-ranked plan (media_plan) combines poster (a channel research.md itself says has no quantitative verification -- §5) with media_relations, so the single-channel TV figure (116) does not represent that plan's actual composite performance either. Calling this a general/universal ('一般的な') strength measured by comparing real events ('実際のイベントで比べた記録') overstates what a single-event, single-channel-level survey can establish about three multi-channel composite plans -- design review r6 flagged this as CORE_CAUSAL_MODEL_DISTORTED/SOURCE_TRACEABILITY_MISMATCH. This correction removes exactly the overreaching framing phrase (the 'general/universal, event-comparison-based' characterization) via pure deletion, leaving the same ordinal ranking (flyer plan > media plan > SNS plan) presented as a plain reference without asserting a specific evidentiary methodology it doesn't have. The tie-break RULE itself (use this disclosed ranking when two plans are otherwise tied) is unchanged -- only the overstated characterization of its evidentiary basis is removed.
